provenance.canvas: crawl4ai ships a light docs mode; canvas set to a warm editorial paper (#f0ede4, ~luma 237) — a deliberate canvas-value flip off the last two dark videos, which also clears the frame-brightness floor by construction
provenance.accent: crawl4ai's teal, deepened for a light canvas. crawl4ai's electric teal (#09b5a5 / #0be5d1) washes out on cream at only 2.2:1 contrast, so the accent is deepened along the same ~173 hue to #0a8175 (a forest-teal) which clears the 3.0:1 accent floor at 4.07:1 while staying recognizably crawl4ai's color. The renderer auto-derives --accent-ink (blended toward ink) for teal-scale TEXT; raw #0a8175 carries the confidence curve, nodes, dots and glow with real contrast on the paper. (The extractor's #0be5d1 was the pushfeedback widget's --feedback-primary-color, not the site's identity.)
provenance.ink: near-black cool ink #14181a (~luma 23) for a light canvas — clears the light-canvas ink floor (<= 60)
provenance.ink_muted: mid-gray #5c6162 (~luma 96) for detail rows; --muted-content derives darker toward ink
provenance.hairline: warm light hairline #d7d1c4 derived off the paper canvas

readability.notes: Light warm-paper canvas (~luma 237). Hero/body text ships as --ink (#14181a, ~luma 23). Dark-canvas type sizes and colors did NOT transfer to light (per CRAFT_LOG) — three readability FAILs were root-caused and fixed in build_html.py so a light canvas ships genuine dark coverage, not thin gray glyphs: (1) panes render as dark code-panels (dark fill, light text) — the dark code blocks inside light docs pages; (2) the big_number hero numeral ships in --ink (a teal --accent-ink hero was bloom-lifted past the light-canvas ceiling); (3) the metaphor core is a solid --ink disc (the decision point the network converges on). Teal identity stays on the confidence curve, dots and glow (raw #0a8175, 4.07:1 on canvas). Final screening: all scenes pass, min luma spread 188, poster std 89.6.
bright_beats: the whole runtime is a bright light frame (mean luma far above the 46 floor) — the operator's 'every video seems dark' complaint is answered by canvas, not grade
the saturated teal confidence curve is the graphic light source / focal pop in scenes 3 and 5 against the warm paper
inverted_beats: none — this is a deliberately all-light editorial run (the whole frame is the bright field). A forced dark inverted scene would reintroduce the exact darkness the canvas flip removes, so the contrast budget is spent on teal saturation against cream, not on a polarity flip. The renderer has no per-scene polarity flag, so a light run stays light; the money shot reads as the peak via the crash_zoom camera, the riser_braam foley button, and the curve reaching full glow on the threshold cross (emphasize).
readability.brightness_plan: Bright light-canvas throughout — mean luma sits far above the 46 floor and every scene clears the bright-scene threshold, so the frame-brightness gate passes by construction. The color script is teal-saturation contrast (the curve and lit nodes pop against warm paper) plus camera dynamics, not a dark/light value swing; the standing 'every video seems dark' note is answered wholesale by the canvas.

color_gate_note: Accent is crawl4ai's teal (hue ~174), only 32 off 07-09's green (142) and 138 off 07-08's amber (36) — the HUE clause alone would FAIL against green. Satisfied instead by the CANVAS-VALUE FLIP: 07-08 and 07-09 were both dark; this run is a light warm-paper canvas (dark->light), which the variety color gate accepts. Temperature also reads differently (a warm paper world vs two dark cool/warm accent worlds).
